lines.text: The moment your front bumper pulls up to a fast-food ordering menu, a chime beeps inside the employee's headset.
It is not a cashier staring out the window or a hidden camera triggering the chime.
Buried beneath the asphalt pavement is an induction loop sensor made of insulated copper wire.
An electrical current runs through the wire loop, creating an invisible electromagnetic field above the driveway.
When thousands of pounds of steel in your car roll overhead, the metal disrupts the coil's magnetic inductance.
The detector registers the frequency shift, triggering the headset chime and starting an automated order timer.
That buried magnetic sensor keeps fast-food drive-through lines moving at lightning speed.
